title: A New Surprising Amazon Live-Action Anime Adaptation Has Been Announced
content:
Streaming services seem to always be looking for new content, with many platforms such as Netflix, Hulu, Tubi, and more always searching for the next big thing. With the popularity of cinematic universes like the MCU, it makes sense that streaming outlets would be looking to established stories to hit the screen. Unsurprisingly, the anime genre has been rife with possibilities, as many studios are aiming to create live-action takes on classic anime tales. To no one’s surprise, Amazon is also looking to capitalize on the live-action anime adaptation department, though the recently confirmed series is one that many anime fans might not be familiar with.

Amazon Prime Video has announced that Please Save My Earth will receive a live-action television series, landing on the platform in the fall of 2027. Attached to star as protagonist Alice Sakaguchi, actor Alice Hirose will help bring this new show to life. Much like Netflix’s One Piece with franchise creator Eiichiro Oda, Amazon is planning to have creator Saki Hiwatari play a big role in bringing the series to life. Specifically, Hiwatari announced that he was acting as a supervisor to the scriptwriting process and is extremely excited to see his work brought to the “real world.” Director Takahiro Miki will be handling the series, having previously worked on projects such as Until We Meet Again and My Undead Yokai Girlfriend .

Will The Earth Be Saved?

Please Save My Earth first debuted as a manga in 1986 by creator Saki Hiwatari, running for almost ten years before bringing its tale to a close. Ironically, the first anime adaptation was only released one year prior to its final chapter, with none other than Production I.G. taking on the task of bringing this story to life via films and OVA specials. The story itself follows high schooler Alice Sakaguchi, who tries babysitting her neighbor Rin Kobayashi, but comes to discover that recent dreams she’s been having are far more than she expected. In fact, the dreams aren’t dreams at all, but rather visions of her past life as an alien scientist. Joined by other students who have the same dreams, Please Save My Earth is a mind-bending story that blends drama and comedy with its wild premise.

Unfortunately, Please Save My Earth’s anime isn’t currently available to stream on any official streaming services, so catching up on the story might prove a little tricky. Ironically enough, this series isn’t the first that Amazon Prime Video was looking to give a live-action adaptation. Previously, the platform confirmed that it was working to create a live-action take on The Promised Neverland , which was initially announced all the way back in 2020. No news has been shared regarding what happened to the adaptation and when it will arrive, so the alien anime tale might beat the children of Grace Field House to the streaming service.

title: Expelled from Paradise Visual Novel's Teaser Trailer Reveals November 26 Release
content:
Toei Animation began streaming on Friday a new teaser trailer for it and developer Studio51 Inc.'s Expelled from Paradise -The Stellar Angel- ( Rakuen Tsuihō -The Stellar Angel- ), a visual novel in the Expelled from Paradise franchise , and it reveals that the game will launch on November 26 for Nintendo Switch and PC via Steam .

The game is getting an English release . The game will have support in English and Japanese.

Toei Animation is the publisher and it describes the game's story:

A brand-new sequel depicting the aftermath of the theatrical anime Expelled from Paradise . The story of Angela and Dingo begins to move once more. This is a full-scale visual novel that weaves a grand sci-fi vision through evocative text and immersive direction.

The film reunites the main staff of Expelled from Paradise , including director Seiji Mizushima , scriptwriter Gen Urobuchi of Nitroplus , character designer Masatsugu Saitō , and composer NARASAKI . Toei Animation is producing the animation.

While the original announcement of the film had featured the title Rakuen Tsuihō : Liberated from Paradise , a later announcement listed the title as Rakuen Tsuihō -Expelled from Paradise- Kokoro no Resonance as well as Rakuen Tsuihō: Kokoro no Resonance instead.

Expelled from Paradise debuted in 13 theaters in Japan in November 2014, and sold 110,000 tickets. The film's Blu-ray Disc and DVD release in Japan sold more than 70,000 copies. The film won the Best Animation of the Year Award at the 24th Japan Movie Critics Awards in May 2015.

Aniplex of America released Expelled from Paradise in 15 theaters across the United States in December 2014. The company then released the film on Blu-ray Disc in North, Central, and South America in June 2015.

The film returned to theaters in Japan in November 2024 in 4K resolution as Expelled from Paradise -Impelled by 10th Anniversary- to commemorate the film's 10-year anniversary.

title: My Hero Academia Returns With New Merch For 10th Anniversary After Its True Finale
content:
Although My Hero Academia has already reached its conclusion, the series continues to stay in the spotlight thanks to its 10th anniversary celebrations. Based on the acclaimed manga written and illustrated by Kohei Horikoshi, Studio Bones released an anime adaptation in 2016, which later became one of the most successful series of all time. With more than 100 million manga copies in circulation and a globally famous anime adaptation, My Hero Academia ‘s success is nothing less than historic. While the anime wrapped up the main story in December last year, it returned with two new episodes as part of the anniversary celebrations.

However, even if the anime has no plans to return, the anniversary celebrations continue with more exciting projects. An official website was launched for this milestone to share all the updates regarding the anniversary projects and releases. The series is returning with Class 1-A figures, which include all the students, All Might, and Shota Aizawa. They’re wearing formal attire instead of their usual hero costumes, since it was designed specifically for the 10th anniversary. The individual figures were placed together to hype up the latest release. They will be available individually in crane games across Japan in 2027. So far, these figures have not been confirmed for a U.S. release.

My Hero Academia Released Its True Finale This Month

While the anime concluded its main story in December 2025, the series already confirmed its return with a special episode. My Hero Academia is one of those rare series that received a complete adaptation, and it’s all thanks to its popularity. The special episode, My Hero Academia: More , adapted the extra chapter from the final volume, which followed the beloved characters eight years after the final war. A few months after the special episode, an anime short, I Am a Hero Too , was released on August 2nd, 2026.

This six-minute short was based on a one-shot by Kohei Horikoshi from the 2025 fanbook My Hero Academia: Ultra-Age . Centering on teenage Eri, the short bids a heartwarming farewell to fans who have been part of the journey for several years. After the latest short’s release, the anime doesn’t have any canon material left to adapt. While the anime may never return with a new story by Horikishi, the series’ legacy will live on thanks to new projects and releases.

My Hero Academia ‘s 10th Anniversary Continues Its Celebrations

Both the special episode and the anime short were part of the anniversary celebrations, but the series has planned more surprises than that. The series has been in the spotlight for several months thanks to the latest projects. One of the most exciting projects is the Exhibition , which will be held in Tokyo in February 2027. The same exhibition will also move on to Osaka, where fans can witness the life-size figures of the beloved characters. Additionally, the exhibition will shed light on the story’s trajectory. Just like a majority of the exhibitions, it will only be held in Japan.

title: Dark Horse to Release Vampire Hunter D: Rose Princess Manga, Vampire Hunter D: Fortress of Blood Comic, The Case of Charles Dexter Ward Manga (Updated)
content:
Dark Horse Manga announced at Anime NYC on Friday that it will release two graphic novels in Hideyuki Kikuchi and Yoshitaka Amano 's Vampire Hunter D franchise . The company will release the Vampire Hunter D : Fortress of Blood comic on December 16 and will release the English translation of Vampire Hunter D : Rose Princess , Saiko Takaki 's manga adaptation of the ninth novel "The Rose Princess," in March 2027. The company also revealed that it will release Gou Tanabe 's manga adaptation of H.P. Lovecraft 's The Case of Charles Dexter Ward ( Charles Ward no Kikai na Jiken ) horror novella in early 2027.

Writer Chris Condon ( That Texas Blood, Ultimate Wolverine ) and artist Filipe Andrade ( The Many Deaths of Laila Starr, Rare Flavours ) will create the Vampire Hunter D : Fortress of Blood comic series. Jordie Bellaire ( Six of Us, Assassin's Apprentice ) is the colorist and Frank Cvetkovic ( Kingdom of Earth, Batman: Dark Patterns ) the letterer. Andrade is drawing the main cover art and Riccardo Federici ( The Last God ), and original Vampire Hunter D cover artist, illustrator, and designer Yoshitaka Amano are drawing variant covers. Subsequent issues will include cover art from Emma Rios, Dan Quintana, and Eliza Ivanova.

The comic book series is listed as a four-issue series. The first issue will retail for US$4.99.

Dark Horse Manga describes its story:

A vampire lord has marshalled his forces and is marching on human settlements, aiming to leave no survivors! The old fortress stands in his path to the next city, and within it is a family of outcasts who must buy enough time for humans to flee from the bloodbath. Wandering that same path is the indomitable hunter, the terrifyingly beautiful half-human, half-vampire known as D.

Dark Horse shared a quote from Kikuchi:

"I am deeply honored to finally see the adaptation of D into an American comic book. I never could have imagined that D, a series born in Japan, would be reborn in the form of an American Comic. I would like to express my gratitude to Dark Horse Comics for making this a reality, and above all, to the people that help make it happen, Michael Gombos , the editor, Judy Khuu , as well as to Filipe Andrade, who created the wonderful illustrations, and Chris Condon, who crafted a superb script tailored for the American comic book format from my original scenario! I hope that this comic will serve as a catalyst for the story of D to spread beyond Japan and the United States, and reach the entire world."

Kevin Leahy is translating the manga into English.

Dark Horse Manga describes its story:

The village of Sacri is a fertile oasis on the otherwise barren frontier. But Sacri's prosperity comes at a steep price! The ruling noble, an immortal vampire princess, feasts on the villagers at her whim. When a young man attempts to save his lover from being bitten, the princess sends her four savage knights to punish the petulant villagers. Standing in their way is none other than the beautiful and dangerous Vampire Hunter D ! With the help of a rebellious young woman named Elena, D undertakes a quest to end the princess's deadly rule. But first, the two of them will risk their lives in an epic duel with her knights.

Takaki launched the manga adaptation of the overall novel series in 2007. Digital Manga Publishing released seven volumes of the manga digitally and in print. Kadokawa later released the eighth and final compiled book volume of the manga in English digitally and in print.

Unified Pictures announced in April it is adapting new volumes of the Vampire Hunter D novels into a 20-issue comic book series by Brandon Easton and Ryan Benjamin. The company stated in April the comic series would debut in summer 2026.

Kikuchi launched the original novel series in January 1983. Asahi Sonorama began publishing the novels in 2005. The 57th volume of the novel series shipped on January 7. Graphic Audio published audiobook adaptations of the novels in 2021. Dark Horse Comics is releasing the novels in English, and released the first three novels in an omnibus volume in October 2021.

Kikuchi's novels inspired the Vampire Hunter D original video anime ( OVA ) in 1985 and the Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust film in 2000. Sentai Filmworks most recently released the OVA on DVD and Blu-ray Disc in 2015, and Discotek Media most recently released Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust on DVD and Blu-ray Disc in 2015. Iconic Events Releasing and Anime Expo 's AX Cinema Nights program hosted the 40th anniversary screenings of the OAV in April 2025. HIDIVE and Shudder began streaming the OVA in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand in May 2025.

The original story follows Marinus Bicknell Willett, the doctor for the noted Ward family of Rhode Island, investigating the case of the supposed madness of the young Charles Dexter Ward. His investigation leads to a grim discovery of the Ward family's mysterious and horrific past, and Charles Ward's involvement in it hundreds of years later.

The semimonthly manga series is part of a series of adaptations of H.P. Lovecraft 's works by Tanabe. Dark Horse Comics published his manga of H.P. Lovecraft's The Hound and Other Stories in August 2017, which includes "The Hound," "The Temple," and "The Nameless City." Dark Horse Comics began releasing Tanabe's At The Mountains Of Madness manga in June 2019. The series was nominated for Best Comic by the 46th Angoulême International Comics Festival in 2019.

Dark Horse has also released a single omnibus volume of Tanabe's The Shadow Over Innsmouth manga, and has also released Tanabe's The Call of Cthulhu manga, the latter of which won the Superior Achievement in a Graphic Novel award at the Bram Stoker Awards in June 2025. Dark Horse more recently released Tanabe's The Colour Out of Space last July, and released The Shadow Out of Time on December 16. Dark Horse will release The Dunwich Horror manga on September 29.

Tanabe also released manga based on Lovecraft's The Haunter of the Dark and The Outsider .

Tanabe launched the Short Stories about Dreamlands manga based on H.P. Lovecraft 's Dream Cycle stories in November 2023, and ended the series in April 2024. Tanabe launched the Lovecraft no Genei (The Lovecraft's Phantom) manga in Comic Beam in June 2024, and ended it in December 2024.

contentBlocks.text: Dark Horse Manga announced at Anime NYC on Friday that it will release two graphic novels in Hideyuki Kikuchi and Yoshitaka Amano 's Vampire Hunter D franchise . The company will release the Vampire Hunter D : Fortress of Blood comic on December 16 and will release the English translation of Vampire Hunter D : Rose Princess , Saiko Takaki 's manga adaptation of the ninth novel "The Rose Princess," in March 2027.

Writer Chris Condon ( That Texas Blood, Ultimate Wolverine ) and artist Filipe Andrade ( The Many Deaths of Laila Starr, Rare Flavours ) will create the Vampire Hunter D : Fortress of Blood comic series. Jordie Bellaire ( Six of Us, Assassin's Apprentice ) is the colorist and Frank Cvetkovic ( Kingdom of Earth, Batman: Dark Patterns ) the letterer. Andrade is drawing the main cover art and Riccardo Federici ( The Last God ), and original Vampire Hunter D cover artist, illustrator, and designer Yoshitaka Amano are drawing variant covers. Subsequent issues will include cover art from Emma Rios, Dan Quintana, and Eliza Ivanova.
The comic book series is listed as a four-issue series. The first issue will retail for US$4.99.
Dark Horse Manga describes its story:

A vampire lord has marshalled his forces and is marching on human settlements, aiming to leave no survivors! The old fortress stands in his path to the next city, and within it is a family of outcasts who must buy enough time for humans to flee from the bloodbath. Wandering that same path is the indomitable hunter, the terrifyingly beautiful half-human, half-vampire known as D.
Dark Horse shared a quote from Kikuchi:

"I am deeply honored to finally see the adaptation of D into an American comic book. I never could have imagined that D, a series born in Japan, would be reborn in the form of an American Comic. I would like to express my gratitude to Dark Horse Comics for making this a reality, and above all, to the people that help make it happen, Michael Gombos , the editor, Judy Khuu , as well as to Filipe Andrade, who created the wonderful illustrations, and Chris Condon, who crafted a superb script tailored for the American comic book format from my original scenario! I hope that this comic will serve as a catalyst for the story of D to spread beyond Japan and the United States, and reach the entire world."

contentBlocks.credit: Image courtesy of Dark Horse Manga

contentBlocks.text: Kevin Leahy is translating the manga into English.
Dark Horse Manga describes its story:

The village of Sacri is a fertile oasis on the otherwise barren frontier. But Sacri's prosperity comes at a steep price! The ruling noble, an immortal vampire princess, feasts on the villagers at her whim. When a young man attempts to save his lover from being bitten, the princess sends her four savage knights to punish the petulant villagers. Standing in their way is none other than the beautiful and dangerous Vampire Hunter D ! With the help of a rebellious young woman named Elena, D undertakes a quest to end the princess's deadly rule. But first, the two of them will risk their lives in an epic duel with her knights.

Takaki launched the manga adaptation of the overall novel series in 2007. Digital Manga Publishing released seven volumes of the manga digitally and in print. Kadokawa later released the eighth and final compiled book volume of the manga in English digitally and in print.

Unified Pictures announced in April it is adapting new volumes of the Vampire Hunter D novels into a 20-issue comic book series by Brandon Easton and Ryan Benjamin. The company stated in April the comic series would debut in summer 2026.

Kikuchi launched the original novel series in January 1983. Asahi Sonorama began publishing the novels in 2005. The 57th volume of the novel series shipped on January 7. Graphic Audio published audiobook adaptations of the novels in 2021. Dark Horse Comics is releasing the novels in English, and released the first three novels in an omnibus volume in October 2021.

Kikuchi's novels inspired the Vampire Hunter D original video anime ( OVA ) in 1985 and the Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust film in 2000. Sentai Filmworks most recently released the OVA on DVD and Blu-ray Disc in 2015, and Discotek Media most recently released Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust on DVD and Blu-ray Disc in 2015. Iconic Events Releasing and Anime Expo 's AX Cinema Nights program hosted the 40th anniversary screenings of the OAV in April 2025. HIDIVE and Shudder began streaming the OVA in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, and New Zealand in May 2025.

title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2 Trailer Hints at a Very Different Story
content:
Cyberpunk: Edgerunners will continue to explore the animated world of Night City, fleshing out the universe that first started with CD Projekt Red’s video game, Cyberpunk 2077 . The first season, at this point, is considered anime royalty by many fans, as the story of David and Lucy resonated deeply with many. Thanks to the conclusion of Edgerunners’ first season, seeing these star-crossed lovers return was always a long shot, though the latest trailer for season two appears to be swinging in a wild new direction. Set to arrive this October, the second season proves that the more things change in Night City, the more they stay the same.

One major commonality that the two seasons of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners share isn’t just the focus on Night City’s residents and this futuristic setting, but the Edgerunner class making a return. However, rather than focusing on an aspiring Edgerunner like David, the second season focuses on a character named “Weak Kingsley.” Weak has already become a legend of Night City, mostly living without the technology that brought him to the top of the food chain. Unfortunately, it seems as though Kingsley is going to be dragged back into the world he once left behind, leaving many to wonder if he’ll face the same tragic ending that David experienced in season one. You can check out the brand-new trailer below.

Cyberpunk: From Rags to Riches

Cyberpunk as a franchise has gone through some wild years since the video game first hit personal computers and consoles. Following numerous delays, Cyberpunk 2077 released in 2020, giving fans an experience that many fans weren’t prepared for. While CD Projekt Red did give fans a living, breathing world to explore in the digital landscape, the game was originally littered with technical glitches that caused many to stay away from Night City at the start. Ironically enough, a big part of what helped resurrect the game was the arrival of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners itself.

Cyberpunk: Edgerunners arrived on Netflix in 2022 , brought to life by none other than the legendary production house Studio TRIGGER. For those who need a refresher, TRIGGER has been responsible for amazing anime outings including Kill la Kill, Promare, and Delicious in Dungeon . So big was Edgerunners that CD Projekt began adding characters and elements from the anime directly into the video game, helping to spark a resurgence of players who were willing to give the digital outing a whirl. At present, the video game producer hasn’t confirmed if elements from Edgerunners season two will arrive in 2077, though we certainly wouldn’t be surprised, considering how the anime adaptation worked in tandem to help the game hit new heights. Luckily, we can all check out the second season when it lands on Netflix on October 20th .

title: Yen Press Licenses The Goblin Samurai, My Crush's Crush Manga
content:
Yen Press announced at Anime NYC on Friday that it has licensed the following manga ( Yen Press did not reveal the release date for the titles):

Title: The Goblin Samurai Creator: Kikurage Synopsis: There are legends of a nameless goblin swordsman. Missing one eye, with no mastery of magic, and born from a low-ranking tribe, yet he is well-spoken—and a warrior of peerless skill. With grace that matches his peerless swordplay, the tale of this wanderer from another world begins!

Title: My Crush's Crush ( Boku no Suki na Hito ga Suki na Hito ) Creator: Sekina Aoi (writer), Ryō Tsuzura (author) Synopsis: When Sora Akizuki confesses his feelings to Miya Fuwa, he gets rejected outright. As it turns out, she likes Asahi Suzukaze, the president of the mysterious “Clinical Trials Club.” When he joins the club to learn more about Asahi, he discovers that she also has a crush on someone else! Could this chain of crushes get any more complicated...?

Yen Press also announced that it will release an audiobook of The Boy and The Beast light novel, and the Rise of the Lowborn: Ascending the Ranks by Crushing Incompetent Nobles light novel. Yen Press had announced its license of the Rise of the Lowborn: Ascending the Ranks by Crushing Incompetent Nobles novel series in May. Yen Press will debut the novel series in print in November.

title: Avatar: The Last Airbender’s Zuko Movie Might Have Been Canceled For a Controversial Reason
content:
Following the successful run of Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender on Paramount+, there’s plenty for bending enthusiasts to look forward to. Avatar: Seven Havens will land on the streaming service this October, focusing on the Avatar who succeeds Korra, with the co-creators of the Nickelodeon franchise teasing another series in the works. Unfortunately, for those hoping for more movies to follow Avatar Aang’s lead, Paramount has bad news for you. In recent reports, it appears as though the now-defunct animated film focusing on Fire Lord Zuko has been canceled, and fans might ultimately be surprised to learn why.

Reportedly, the canceled animated film would have followed Zuko after the original series finale and would have explored the origins of the “Red Lotus.” For those who might need a refresher, the Red Lotus organization was an anarchistic band of benders that made landfall in the third season of The Legend of Korra. With each member of the team being a skilled bender, including the nefarious airbender Zaheer, they made for one of the biggest challenges Korra had to face. In a recent report, Paramount seemingly canceled the film because of its more mature, darker political tone. The studio hasn’t commented on the defunct movie or why it was canceled, though fans are sharing their thoughts on the cancellation.

Will Zuko Return?

As Avatar fans know, the recent animated film did have a significant role for Zuko to play. While Dante Basco didn’t return to reprise his role in Avatar Aang , Steven Yeun, from The Walking Dead and Invincible , took on the part of the Fire Lord. Zuko fans might have been disappointed to see that he didn’t play a larger role, as the animated movie mostly focused on Aang and his issues in coming to grips with the loss of the airbenders, but the movie still had plenty of battles for Zuko to take part in. While Zuko is sure to be a big part of Netflix’s live-action adaptation for its third and final season, his animated future is anyone’s guess.

Avatar: Seven Havens takes place following the passing of Korra, meaning that it is happening decades after the events of Avatar Aang. At this point in the timeline, Zuko is long dead, though this doesn’t necessarily mean that we won’t see him make an appearance in the sequel series. One of the benefits of the Avatar franchise has been its ability to drift into the “spirit realm,” which has offered fans the opportunity to see deceased characters make a comeback, albeit in unexpected ways. In The Legend of Korra, for example, we saw Uncle Iroh return thanks to the world of spirits, encountering the titular character, so the same could be true for a potential Zuko comeback.

title: The Fate of Every Hashira in Demon Slayer Explained
content:
Warning: This article contains spoilers from the Demon Slayer manga! Right after the finale of the Hashira Training Arc , Demon Slayer announced a trilogy of films to adapt the Infinity Castle Arc , the longest and most intense arc in the manga. The final phase of the manga is split into two parts: the Infinity Castle and the Sunrise Countdown . While it’s unclear if the Sunrise Countdown will be adapted into a movie or a TV season, at the very least, fans can expect to enjoy all the exciting fights in the Infinity Castle Arc on the big screen. The anime released the first installment of the trilogy last year, and it became a smashing hit all across the globe.

However, while the anime has yet to adapt a majority of the story, the manga has long since reached its conclusion. Demon Slayer ‘s finale was extremely controversial at the time due to many tragic deaths that happened during the final battle against the demons. As the strongest in the entire Corps, the Hashira have always been on the front lines, and the final battle wasn’t any different.

9) Kyojuro Rengoku

Rengoku is the first Hashira to die in the series, and it happened long before the final battle. During the Mugen Train Arc , Tanjiro and the others joined him on a mission to defeat the demon responsible for the missing passengers inside the Infinity Train. As the Flame Hashira, it goes without saying just how powerful Rengoku was. However, even his overwhelming strength wasn’t enough against the Third Upper Moon. While the mission itself was a huge success with no casualties, no one anticipated the appearance of Akaza.

Not to mention, he wasn’t anything like the Lower Moons, and the difference in their powers was astounding. Rengoku made sure that no one else would have to fight the Upper Three and held on until dawn. Even with a hole in his chest, Rengoku adjusted his breathing and kept fighting to protect everyone until the end. His death is one of the most emotional moments in the series as it gives Tanjiro and the others the push they needed to become stronger.

8) Tengen Uzui

As the Sound Hashira, Uzui had a crucial role in the Entertainment District Arc. Right after the Mugen Train Arc, when Tanjiro and his friends were training diligently, they came across Uzui, who was looking for lower-ranking Demon Slayers to help with a mission. Following a series of events, Uzui and the others ended up fighting Upper Moon Six, Gyutaro, who shared his powers with his sister Daki. The fight was brutal, and the animation is still unmatched .

He suffered grave injuries, including poisoning, losing his left hand and eye. As a dual sword wielder, continuing to work as a Demon Slayer would’ve been increasingly difficult. Although he could’ve chosen to go down the dangerous path, he decided to retire peacefully and live the rest of his life with his wives. As a Shinobi turned Demon Slayer, Uzui spent most of his life fighting, but he finally managed to live on his own terms. He continued to help the Corps out with training and protecting Nezuko during the battle.

7) Shinobu Kocho

Shinobu is not only the Insect Hashira, but also the backbone of the Corps thanks to her extensive knowledge of poisons and medical treatment. Her Butterfly Mansion houses the injured Slayers, where she oversees their treatment and rehabilitation. This makes her one of the most crucial figures in the Corps. Her biggest goal was to find a way to defeat Doma, the Upper Rank Two who killed her sister. Shinobu came face to face with the demon in the Infinity Castle Arc. It was the first major fight in the entire arc, and it ended with her tragic death.

Despite giving it her all, she was unable to defeat the demon and ended up being absorbed by him. That horrifying scene was witnessed by Kanao Tsuyuri , her Tsuguko and adoptive sister. Even after her death, she continues to remain relevant in the story as her real plan comes to light. It wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say that without her, Doma and Muzan’s defeat might have been impossible.

6) Muichiro Tokito

Although Muichiro is the youngest Hashira , his potential is better than most of the cast thanks to his lineage of being a direct descendant of the Sun Breathing Technique. During the Swordsmith Village Arc, he regained his memories and mourned the family he once had. He also awakened his Demon Slayer Mark and effortlessly killed Gyokko, the Upper Rank Five. Considering how much trouble Gyutaro gave to Uzui and the others, Muichiro’s victory was nothing short of marvelous. Just like the rest of the Demon Slayers, he was trapped inside the Infinity Castle, where he used his new powers against Upper One.

It goes without saying that the second most powerful demon in history was more than he could handle. Even with the help of Sanemi, Gyomei, and Genya, the fight was overly intense. Muichiro had one of the most brutal deaths in the series as Kokushibo cut him in half. Even in his dying breath, he landed one final blow to the villain, which paved the path for others to defeat him. After the Infinity Castle collapsed, the surviving Demon Slayers engaged in a battle against Muzan, leaving them with no chance of retrieving the young Hashira’s body.

5) Mitsuri Kanroji

Mitsuri is another Hashira who joined the battle against the Upper Moons in the Swordsmith Village Arc. While Muichiro defeated Gyokko, Mitsuri helped Tanjiro and the others against Hantengu, the Upper Four. She also awakened her Demon Slayer Mark during the battle, which basically saved her life from the powerful demon. She was one of the few survivors in the Infinity Castle Arc, but her luck ran out during the battle against Muzan Kibutsuji. She sustained severe injuries and blood loss because of the demon progenitor.

Not only that, but both her arms were sliced off, leaving her unable to continue fighting. She managed to stay alive for a little while until Obanai returned to her after fighting Muzan. While she couldn’t live the rest of her life with him like she wanted, she confessed her feelings to him, hoping to marry Obanai if they ever got reincarnated. After she heard Obanai promise her that, she drew her final breath in his arms.

4) Obanai Iguro

Obanai and Mitsuri were together the entire time they were trapped inside the Infinity Castle. They fought against Nakime, the newly appointed Upper Four, whose Blood Demon Art manifested the Infinity Castle. After the Infinity Castle Arc, Obanai joined the others during the final battle against Muzan. He also witnessed Mitsuri’s weakened state and knew she wouldn’t survive all those horrifying injuries. Despite knowing he wouldn’t survive the battle, he charged towards Muzan, hoping to do as much damage as possible. Obanai lost his eyesight because of the villain but never stopped fighting him.

His Demon Slayer Mark gave him a slight edge, but it wasn’t enough to help him survive. After the battle was over, he reunited with Mitsuri and succumbed to his injuries a few moments later. They both died at the same time after making a promise that was the only hope they wanted to hold on to, even though they knew it might never come true.

3) Gyomei Himejima

While the anime has long since confirmed that Gyomei is the strongest Hashira, the Infinity Castle Arc will finally explain the true extent of his overwhelming powers. Gyomei teamed with Muichiro, Sanemi, and Genya to fight the Upper Rank One. Kokushibo has been alive for a few centuries, and he’s easily the most powerful demon after Muzan. Kokushibo’s powers were unlike anything the other Upper Ranks were capable of, including Doma and Akaza. He awakened his Demon Slayer Mark even though he was past the lethal age, which meant that his time was limited.

While he survived the battle against Kokushibo, Gyomei suffered severe injuries during his fight with Muzan. He lost his leg on top of other injuries and blood loss. Despite that, he ensured that he kept Muzan chained down until sunrise. Gyomei drew his final breath after the battle was over. He also regained his memories of the time he took care of orphans. After remembering that the children didn’t betray him but wanted to protect him from the demon instead, he finally gained peace after all these years.

2) Sanemi Shinazugawa

Sanemi is one of the few surviving Corps members, but the series never revealed if he died after he turned 25. Sanemi was only 21 years old at the time, so he could’ve still had a few years to live. He awakened his Demon Slayer Mark during the battle against Kokushibo, and his efforts ensured the demon’s victory. However, Sanemi also lost the only family he had and carried the weight of that loss for the rest of his life.

While Sanemi kept pushing Genya away to protect him, all the younger brother wanted was his forgiveness. Sanemi also fought against Muzan during the final battle and lived to see the demon’s demise. After the Corps was disbanded, he lived the rest of his days in peace while keeping in touch with Tanjiro through letters.

1) Giyu Tomioka

Giyu is another Hashira who survived the battle against Muzan. Following his battle against Akaza, Giyu and Tanjiro were both unable to continue fighting other demons for a while. However, after the Infinity Castle collapsed, Giyu once again used his powers to protect as many people as he could. He joined hands with Tanjiro once again to defeat the final villain and sustained severe injuries in the process. Giyu also lost his arm, but he never gave up fighting.

The night-long battle ended in the Corps’ victory, but barely anyone survived to celebrate the historic moment. Just like Sanemi, Giyu was also 21 years old at the time, so it’s hinted that he could’ve died in four years. However, the series never officially confirmed his death, and much about the Mark and its history isn’t known either. Following the disbandment of the Corps, he lived a solitary life while keeping in touch with his former comrades.

Shinobu is not only the Insect Hashira, but also the backbone of the Corps thanks to her extensive knowledge of poisons and medical treatment. Her Butterfly Mansion houses the injured Slayers, where she oversees their treatment and rehabilitation. This makes her one of the most crucial figures in the Corps. Her biggest goal was to find a way to defeat Doma, the Upper Rank Two who killed her sister. Shinobu came face to face with the demon in the Infinity Castle Arc. It was the first major fight in the entire arc, and it ended with her tragic death.

Despite giving it her all, she was unable to defeat the demon and ended up being absorbed by him. That horrifying scene was witnessed by Kanao Tsuyuri , her Tsuguko and adoptive sister. Even after her death, she continues to remain relevant in the story as her real plan comes to light. It wouldn’t be an exaggeration to say that without her, Doma and Muzan’s defeat might have been impossible.
6) Muichiro Tokito

Although Muichiro is the youngest Hashira , his potential is better than most of the cast thanks to his lineage of being a direct descendant of the Sun Breathing Technique. During the Swordsmith Village Arc, he regained his memories and mourned the family he once had. He also awakened his Demon Slayer Mark and effortlessly killed Gyokko, the Upper Rank Five. Considering how much trouble Gyutaro gave to Uzui and the others, Muichiro’s victory was nothing short of marvelous. Just like the rest of the Demon Slayers, he was trapped inside the Infinity Castle, where he used his new powers against Upper One.

It goes without saying that the second most powerful demon in history was more than he could handle. Even with the help of Sanemi, Gyomei, and Genya, the fight was overly intense. Muichiro had one of the most brutal deaths in the series as Kokushibo cut him in half. Even in his dying breath, he landed one final blow to the villain, which paved the path for others to defeat him. After the Infinity Castle collapsed, the surviving Demon Slayers engaged in a battle against Muzan, leaving them with no chance of retrieving the young Hashira’s body.
5) Mitsuri Kanroji

Mitsuri is another Hashira who joined the battle against the Upper Moons in the Swordsmith Village Arc. While Muichiro defeated Gyokko, Mitsuri helped Tanjiro and the others against Hantengu, the Upper Four. She also awakened her Demon Slayer Mark during the battle, which basically saved her life from the powerful demon. She was one of the few survivors in the Infinity Castle Arc, but her luck ran out during the battle against Muzan Kibutsuji. She sustained severe injuries and blood loss because of the demon progenitor.

Not only that, but both her arms were sliced off, leaving her unable to continue fighting. She managed to stay alive for a little while until Obanai returned to her after fighting Muzan. While she couldn’t live the rest of her life with him like she wanted, she confessed her feelings to him, hoping to marry Obanai if they ever got reincarnated. After she heard Obanai promise her that, she drew her final breath in his arms.
4) Obanai Iguro

Obanai and Mitsuri were together the entire time they were trapped inside the Infinity Castle. They fought against Nakime, the newly appointed Upper Four, whose Blood Demon Art manifested the Infinity Castle. After the Infinity Castle Arc, Obanai joined the others during the final battle against Muzan. He also witnessed Mitsuri’s weakened state and knew she wouldn’t survive all those horrifying injuries. Despite knowing he wouldn’t survive the battle, he charged towards Muzan, hoping to do as much damage as possible. Obanai lost his eyesight because of the villain but never stopped fighting him.

His Demon Slayer Mark gave him a slight edge, but it wasn’t enough to help him survive. After the battle was over, he reunited with Mitsuri and succumbed to his injuries a few moments later. They both died at the same time after making a promise that was the only hope they wanted to hold on to, even though they knew it might never come true.
3) Gyomei Himejima

While the anime has long since confirmed that Gyomei is the strongest Hashira, the Infinity Castle Arc will finally explain the true extent of his overwhelming powers. Gyomei teamed with Muichiro, Sanemi, and Genya to fight the Upper Rank One. Kokushibo has been alive for a few centuries, and he’s easily the most powerful demon after Muzan. Kokushibo’s powers were unlike anything the other Upper Ranks were capable of, including Doma and Akaza. He awakened his Demon Slayer Mark even though he was past the lethal age, which meant that his time was limited.

While he survived the battle against Kokushibo, Gyomei suffered severe injuries during his fight with Muzan. He lost his leg on top of other injuries and blood loss. Despite that, he ensured that he kept Muzan chained down until sunrise. Gyomei drew his final breath after the battle was over. He also regained his memories of the time he took care of orphans. After remembering that the children didn’t betray him but wanted to protect him from the demon instead, he finally gained peace after all these years.
2) Sanemi Shinazugawa

Sanemi is one of the few surviving Corps members, but the series never revealed if he died after he turned 25. Sanemi was only 21 years old at the time, so he could’ve still had a few years to live. He awakened his Demon Slayer Mark during the battle against Kokushibo, and his efforts ensured the demon’s victory. However, Sanemi also lost the only family he had and carried the weight of that loss for the rest of his life.

While Sanemi kept pushing Genya away to protect him, all the younger brother wanted was his forgiveness. Sanemi also fought against Muzan during the final battle and lived to see the demon’s demise. After the Corps was disbanded, he lived the rest of his days in peace while keeping in touch with Tanjiro through letters.
1) Giyu Tomioka

Giyu is another Hashira who survived the battle against Muzan. Following his battle against Akaza, Giyu and Tanjiro were both unable to continue fighting other demons for a while. However, after the Infinity Castle collapsed, Giyu once again used his powers to protect as many people as he could. He joined hands with Tanjiro once again to defeat the final villain and sustained severe injuries in the process. Giyu also lost his arm, but he never gave up fighting.

The night-long battle ended in the Corps’ victory, but barely anyone survived to celebrate the historic moment. Just like Sanemi, Giyu was also 21 years old at the time, so it’s hinted that he could’ve died in four years. However, the series never officially confirmed his death, and much about the Mark and its history isn’t known either. Following the disbandment of the Corps, he lived a solitary life while keeping in touch with his former comrades.
